adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Movements of arms and wrists; cymbals used in Bhortal.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Movements of the hips are characteristic in Bihu.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Squats and bends included in Bihu.
movement_profile.partnering: Men and women dance together but maintain separate gender roles.
movement_profile.posture: Upright with specific hip, arm, and wrist movements.

signature_moves.description: Complex, colorful patterns created using cymbals.
signature_moves.name: Bhortal Cymbal Patterns

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Rapid changes in pace and rhythm.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid mimicking ritualistic movements without community guidance.

music_profile.musical_form: Traditional folk songs handed down for generations.
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Formal rhythmic compositions called seus in Bihu; fast beat in Bhortal.
music_profile.sound_description: A blend of rhythmic percussion from the dhol and mandal, punctuated by the plaintive, high-pitched notes of the pepa or flute, and the metallic clatter of cymbals.
music_profile.vocal_style: Chorus singing in Ojapali; singing in Bihu.

basic_steps: Bihu: Rhythmic hip and wrist rotation
Jhumur: Synchronous forward and backward leg movement while holding waists
teaching.formation: Group-based; Bihu uses lines and circles; Thiyo Naam requires 25-30 people.
teaching.level_notes: Beginner: Basic rhythmic footwork. Intermediate: Coordination with instruments. Advanced: Ritualistic or complex cymbal patterns.
teaching.rhythm: Varies by dance; Bihu uses formal rhythmic compositions called seus; Bhortal uses a fast beat called Zhiya Nom.
